title: Epistolae
author: Claudianus Mamertus
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0089a.stoa002.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: ad extremum nemo saeculo meo quae uoluit adfirmare sic ualuit, siquidem, dum sese aduersus eum, quem contra loquitur, ex-. sertat, morum ac studiorum linguae utriusque symbolam iure sibi uindicat. sentit ut Pythagoras, diuidit ut Socrates, explicat ut Plato, inplicat ut Aristoteles, ut Aeschines blanditur, ut Demosthenes irascitur, uernat ut Hortensius, aestuat ut Cethegus, incitat ut Curio, moratur ut Fabius, simulat ut Crassus, dissimulat ut Caesar, suadet \'ut Cato, dissuadet ut Appius, persuadet ut Tullius. iam si ad sacrosanctos patres pro conparatione ueniatur, instruit ut Hieronymus, destruit ut Lactantius, adstruit ut Augustinus, adtollitur ut Hilarius, submittitur ut Ioannes, ut Basilius corripit, ut Gregorius consolatur, ut Orosius adfluit, ut Rufinus stringitur, ut Eusebius narrat, ut Eucherius sollicitat, ut Paulinus prouocat, ut Ambrosius perseuerat.
passages.english: Finally, no one in my age has been so able to affirm what he wished, since, while he exerts himself against the one he speaks against, he rightly claims for himself the contribution of the character and learning of both languages. He thinks like Pythagoras, distinguishes like Socrates, unfolds like Plato, entangles like Aristotle; he coaxes like Aeschines, rages like Demosthenes, blossoms like Hortensius, burns like Cethegus, rouses like Curio, delays like Fabius, feigns like Crassus, dissembles like Caesar, advises like Cato, dissuades like Appius, persuades like Tullius. Now if one comes, for comparison, to the sacrosanct Fathers, he instructs like Jerome, demolishes like Lactantius, builds up like Augustine, is lifted up like Hilary, is lowly like John, rebukes like Basil, consoles like Gregory, flows abundantly like Orosius, is concise like Rufinus, narrates like Eusebius, stirs like Eucherius, challenges like Paulinus, perseveres like Ambrose.
passages.notes: The word split 'ex-. sertat' is read as 'exsertat'; a stray mark before 'ut Cato' is omitted. 'symbolam' is taken as 'share, contribution'. 'Ioannes' is probably John Chrysostom, and 'Gregorius' probably Gregory of Nazianzus; neither identification is certain. 'stringitur' is taken as 'is concise/compressed'. 'submittitur' may mean 'lowers his style' rather than 'is lowly'.
